title: Why a class cannot extend itself
answer: No. A class cannot directly or indirectly extend itself because that would create a cyclic inheritance graph with no valid superclass initialization or type hierarchy. Java detects the cycle at compile time. AeroTopo's `CompilerRulesTest` includes `class Invalid extends Invalid {}` as an intentionally illegal declaration and verifies that the Java compiler reports an error under the project's Java release level.
